text:
jess: opening a triage thread for a Tilde customer LoRA merge we just onboarded. after merge + int4 quant we're seeing embedding shifts and numeric tokenization length changes. putting together a quickpack to debug.

han: ok good. paste a smallest repro pair so we can see the delta.

jess: small example:
```
input: "Invoice: 1,250.00 USD"
baseline embed (FP16 pre-merge): [0.095, -0.021, 0.13, ...]
post-merge+int4 embed: [0.038, -0.089, 0.04, ...]
cos_sim: 0.71 -> 0.49
```

oleg: that's pretty big. did the LoRA modify the final embedding head or normalization?

jess: LoRA only on attention/proj layers, no head changes. we merged with HF tools then quantized with AWQ int4. if I skip quant (FP16 merged) cos_sim ~0.70. so quant looks suspect. also observed tokenizer returning 5 tokens for the numeric string after quant compare to 3 before.

han: numeric token split could explain mismatched embeddings if the model uses token-pos sensitive features. can you run a tokenizer-diff?

jess: running now. also added test matrix: FP16-merged, INT8, INT4-AWQ(symmetric), INT4-AWQ(asymmetric), GPTQ-int4.

qa-bot: quick-eval artifact uploaded:
- dataset: 120 curated customer invoices + 30 synthetic edge cases
- metrics: avg cos_sim (pre->post): FP16 delta 0.01, INT8 delta 0.05, INT4-AWQ(sym) delta 0.18
- tokenizer diffs: 14/150 inputs show token-length deltas (mostly amounts, dates)
- saved: s3://redwood-onboard/tilde/pack-1745558888/{eval.csv, bad_samples.txt, quant_logs/}

oleg: I'll run AWQ with per-channel symmetric and also GPTQ with 128k calibration. try disabling layer folding and see if that improves numeric tokens.

han: record latency and peak mem for each run. customer cares about int4 cost vs FP16 regression tradeoff.

jess: note: prefix cache was on during initial smoke. planning a run with cache disabled to rule out stale KV artifacts.

deploy-bot: s3 upload complete (uploader jess)  3 files to s3://redwood-onboard/tilde/pack-1745558888/

oleg: first AWQ(sym,no-fold) mini-run done: INT4 cos_sim median 0.52, FP16 0.70. token diffs persist on numeric patterns.

han: ok, given quant is causing user-visible drift and tokenizer length changes, recommendation: 1) immediate rollout with FP16 merged to customer while we investigate quant configs, 2) run targeted calibration for numeric tokens (add them to calibration set), 3) explore hybrid: keep embedding head FP16, quantize rest.

jess: love the hybrid idea. I'll prepare FP16-rollback build and docs for CS. drafting a short customer note: what we saw, recommended FP16 temporary, ETA for fix.

oleg: I'll try a hybrid build (embedding head FP16) and run the 200-sample pass.

qa-bot: hybrid run queued. will post metrics once complete.

han: once we have hybrid numbers, I'll help craft cost/latency comparison for the note. keep the customer-facing language short and actionable.

jess: ETA for hybrid run ~90m. will update thread with links to artifacts. thanks all :thumbsup:
